title: Wells Fargo upgrades US AI infrastructure stocks to neutral after chip rout - The Economic Times
text: Agencies Wells Fargo sees improved risk-reward in beaten-down AI infrastructure stocks but warns that slowing capital expenditure could weaken earnings growth by 2028. Wells Fargo upgraded its view on US artificial intelligence infrastructure companies to “neutral” from “negative,” saying a sharp decline in semiconductor stocks had improved the sector’s risk-reward profile despite persistent concerns about slowing AI investment, Reuters reported. Semiconductor shares have fallen about 38% from their June highs, while valuation multiples have contracted significantly. The brokerage said current prices already reflect much of the expected slowdown in AI-related earnings growth. US Markets Powered By As on 11 Nov 2026, 02:17 AM IST S&P 500 Top Gainers Charter Communications 134.52 (10.99%) Take-Two Interactive 224.95 (8.46%) Akamai Technologies 84.23 (4.90%) Global Payments 101.94 (4.27%) Gainers » S&P 500 Top Losers Coterra Energy 32.56 (-8.62%) Moderna 252.30 (-6.21%) NVIDIA 168.28 (-5.82%) First Solar 180.97 (-5.55%) Losers » Also read: Traders raise odds of 50 bps Fed rate hike as CPI rise exceeds expectations “Risk-reward is reasonable,” analysts led by Ohsung Kwon said in a note on Monday. Current semiconductor valuations imply annual earnings growth of roughly 8%, according to Wells Fargo. Live Events Democratic victories in last week’s US midterm elections, including in states where opposition to new data centres has increased, fuelled concerns that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout. The resulting sell-off erased about $3 trillion from the market value of S&P 500 companies. However, Wells Fargo warned that markets have not fully priced in the risk of an earnings downturn in 2028 as capital spending peaks, supply increases and depreciation costs rise.
